items.title: Simmtech steps up SOCAMM investment as BT substrate supply tightens
items.summary: Major package substrate makers, including Samsung Electro-Mechanics (Semco), are concentrating capital spending on large, high-layer-count ABF substrates, while capacity expansion for BT substrates used in memory packaging remains limited. With BT substrate supply tightening and demand for low-power SOCAMM memory modules rising, South Korea's Simmtech could benefit from its business in both memory package substrates and module PCBs.

items.title: Nvidia DSX POD targets AI factories as Microsoft and AWS push modular data centers to the edge
items.summary: Nvidia's newly unveiled DSX POD promises to accelerate AI data-center deployment from months to weeks, joining earlier modular offerings from Microsoft and Amazon Web Services (AWS). While all three rely on prefabricated infrastructure, their computing architectures, power requirements, and target markets reveal fundamentally different strategies.

items.title: Semiconductor equipment is not AI chip growth's biggest bottleneck
items.summary: AI is driving a steady upward revision in chip demand, but semiconductor equipment shortages are not the biggest obstacle to expanding AI chip production, according to industry sources. Instead, talent shortages, factory construction constraints, materials availability, power infrastructure, and funding are emerging as more serious challenges, particularly in the US.

items.title: Skymizer partners with Egis to develop 12nm and 6nm AI accelerators
items.summary: Taiwanese startup Skymizer has formally announced a strategic partnership with Egis Technology to develop Flow (T12), a new-generation AI inference chip. This represents roughly one-tenth the power consumption of a comparable Nvidia H100 deployment.
